newsitem.title: INDIA: Some microbes like it hot.
newsitem.headline: Some microbes like it hot.

text.p: Science has stumbled on a world of microbes which thrive in temperatures too hot for other living organisms, a German scientist said on Tuesday.

A microbe called pyrolobus fararii found deep beneath the seabed of the Atlantic Ocean is unable to grow at 80 degrees Celsius because it finds the temperature too cold, K.O. Stetter, professor of microbiology at the University of Regensburg in Germany, told a seminar in Bombay.
"It grows fastest from 105 degrees up to 113 degrees," Stetter said. "It really likes it hot."
Heat-loving microbes infested terrestrial and deep-sea volcanoes and submarine oil fields, Stetter said.
The German professor was addressing a seminar to mark the 25th anniversary of the Indian research centre of German pharmaceuticals firm Hoechst Marion Roussel.
Another species called pyrodictium abyssi grew fastest at 105 degrees Celsius.
"It is an almost unexplored world (and) what we know is the tip of an iceberg," Stetter said.
Many of these microbes survive autoclaving, a heat-treatment process used by doctors and industries to disinfect equipment, Stetter said.
